Durations (seconds): {value:hms} → 5372:04:37, {value:hm}, {value:dhms} → 223d 20:04:37. Instants (milliseconds since the epoch, datetime type): {value:date}, {value:time}, {value:datetime} — in UTC.

props.name: Name
props.faceplateMissing: This faceplate no longer exists in the project.
props.cutChild: Cut — puts the child back in the page clipboard
props.zonesHint: Accessible zones: comma-separated ids. Empty = no restriction.
props.rangeHint: Empty min/max = exact value match. With either one set, the entry matches by range (min <= value < max) instead of an exact value — max is excluded: with entries 30-40 and 40-50, the value 40 matches the second entry, not the first.
props.rangeGap: gap between this and "{{label}}" (values {{from}}–{{to}} match no entry)
props.langSelectorHint: Automatically lists the project languages (Languages tab).
props.bgUploadHint: Uploads an image into the project's images/ folder: it travels with export, deploy and backups.
props.traceHiddenHint: The trace starts hidden (saved with the project). The operator can still show/hide it on the fly by clicking its legend entry on the chart.
props.ownScaleHint: This trace uses an independent vertical scale, with its own label column on the left — useful when values are a very different order of magnitude from the other traces.
props.alarmBellHint: Clicking always opens the alarm dropdown — no configurable action.
props.recipePanelHint: Lists recipes and lets the operator apply one, same as Menu → Apply recipe.
props.stateLampHint: Same entries as Text list, drawn as a colored dot with its label instead of just text.
props.motionHint: The object translates along the polyline: the tag value maps Min..Max to path start..end. Page coordinates.
props.statesPrecedence: The STATES (N) below take precedence over these colors.
props.motionCapture: Capture from canvas: each click adds a point (Esc to exit)
props.gradientHint: When unset, both ends are derived from the fill colour.
props.ticksHint: 0 = no ticks; with ticks on, min/max are not repeated.
props.matchWidth: Same width as the first selected
props.matchHeight: Same height as the first selected
props.textWrapHint: Text wraps inside Width/Height; hand-written line breaks are kept.
props.barRangeHint: Scale of the stacked bar (sum of segments). Leave Min/Max empty to auto-fit the total; zero is always included (negative values go below the axis).
props.barSeriesScaleHint: Each series has its own Min/Max scale (empty = 0..100). With series on different scales, thresholds and numbered ticks aren't drawn — they'd only describe some bars.
props.pieGroupHint: Group: slices below the given percentage merge into one entry (0 = no grouping). Explode: pulls the largest slice away from the centre.
props.tableHint: Rows scroll inside the declared height: the table no longer overflows its box.
props.ackAllHint: "ACK all" only acknowledges the alarms this object shows (filters and prefix included). Shelving always asks for a reason, recorded in the journal.
props.alarmHistoryHint: Alarm history (activations, acknowledgements, returns) with paging. Leave the filter empty to see them all.
props.soundHint: Different tone per severity; the 🔊 button on the bell silences current alarms (a new one re-enables it). Browsers may block audio until the screen has been touched, and sound is always off in the editor.
props.ackReason: Ask for a reason on acknowledge
props.motionCoordinatesHint: Open these to fix a point by typing the numbers: on the canvas you drag the crosses.
props.targetHint: Decides what the panel puts on screen at the next deploy: the browser or the LVGL viewer. A project with no declared engine is web.
props.targetRiskyConfirm:
SWITCHING TO LVGL

The LVGL engine draws fewer things than the browser: some objects in this project may not appear on the panel — custom symbols, PNG/JPG images, horizontal bars, non-donut pies, and the «Open URL / Login / Logout» button actions.

The other way round (LVGL → web) never loses anything.

Proceed?

cfgUi.variablesNotice: Variables define the project's data points. Link each variable to a register in the {{tab}} section to receive values in real time. Current value is visible only if the runtime is running.
cfgUi.orphanTagsNotice: These tags are active in the protocols but have no variable definition. "Enable history" adds them to the list with history: true — then save.
cfgUi.entityBrowseError: Error: {{error}}. Check that the URL and the token are correct and save the project before browsing.
cfgUi.sourcesNotStartedNotice: ⚠ The sources are not running. This project comes from a template: the addresses below are the example's, and on this network they almost certainly do not exist. Check them, fix them and press Save — from then on the runtime connects.
cfgUi.protocolsNotice: Configure connections to field devices. Supported: Modbus TCP (holding register reads), Modbus RTU (RS-485/RS-232 serial), MQTT (topic subscription), OPC-UA client (subscription, security None), OPC-UA server (exposes SWS tags to higher-level SCADA/MES), HomeAssistant (home-automation sensors and actuators via WebSocket), S7 (Siemens S7-300/400/1200/1500 via ISO-on-TCP port 102), EtherNet/IP (Allen-Bradley ControlLogix/CompactLogix via CIP port 44818). Sources are reconnected in real time on save (no runtime restart).
cfgUi.alarmsNotice: Each alarm watches a variable and activates when the condition is met. Available conditions: above / below (numeric threshold) and bool_equals (for boolean tags). The active state is shown in the top bar of the UI. The Telegram column decides, for each alarm, whether the message goes to the chats configured in Notifications, only to its own chats, or to none.
cfgUi.versioningIntro: Versions this project (project.yaml, synoptics, recipes, history) in a git repository — it never concerns SWS's own code.
cfgUi.usersSavedIn: Users are saved in users.yaml in the project folder. The password is encrypted with Argon2id; the file never contains plain text.
cfgUi.usersDeviceNote: These are the device's users: they travel with the project when you start it and govern access to the panel. The IDE on this PC does not use them and keeps working without asking for credentials.
cfgUi.svgSymbolHelp: Import the symbol's SVG and tick the elements (by id) that must color with the state (off/on/alarm or the object's STATES N). Elements without an id in the SVG cannot be selected: add them in the vector editor.
cfgUi.dbBackupInTab: The full database backup is in the Backup tab: it already includes history/.
cfgUi.odbcNotImplemented: ⚠ The ODBC backend is not implemented: the fields below are saved in the project, but the runtime answers «not compiled in» to every read and write. The real wiring (odbc-api + unixODBC) is postponed until there is an SQL Server or Oracle plant to actually connect.
cfgUi.faceplateIntro: A faceplate is a reusable, parametric graphic block: you define it once here (with parameters such as tag_prefix), then place it as an object on the pages — as many times as you like, each with its own values (e.g. a "motor" block reused for motor1/motor2 by changing only the tag prefix). Unlike a normal object, changing the faceplate here updates all the instances that use it.
cfgUi.faceplateParams: Parameters (one per line): name or name:type=default! — type tag/string/number/color, ! = required
cfgUi.faceplateObjects: Template objects (JSON array — use {{ph}} as a placeholder in the tag/label fields)
cfgUi.recipeIntro: A recipe is a named set of setpoints that are written atomically to the selected tags. Used to change the plant configuration (product change, shift, start-up). Recipes can also be applied from the Runtime View.
cfgUi.smtpNotice: Configure an SMTP server to send emails when an alarm activates. The notify_email and escalate_to fields can be set for each alarm in the Alarms tab.
cfgUi.telegramNotice: Sends a Telegram message when alarms activate and, from scripts, with send_telegram("text"). Create a bot with @BotFather, then paste the token and the destination chat IDs. These are the default chats: in the Alarms tab each alarm can use its own or not notify at all.
cfgUi.telegramStep1: On Telegram open @BotFather → /newbot, follow the instructions and copy the bot's token. Paste it above.
cfgUi.telegramStep2: Send /start (or a message) to the bot; for a group/channel, add it and send a message there.
cfgUi.telegramStep3: Press Detect chats and Add the chats found (groups have a negative ID -100…). Alternatively enter the chat IDs manually.

cfgUi.backupsIntro: Point-in-time snapshots of the project (project.yaml + synoptics + users.yaml + history + recipes) saved under {{dir}}. The runtime creates one automatically every N minutes — by default per the --auto-backup-interval-minutes startup flag, but this project can have its own interval (below), regardless of how the runtime was started.

tipiTab.intro: A type describes once what a motor, a valve or a PID loop looks like. A variable then instantiates it and its parts are reached by path: motore1.velocita. Unit, scaling, limits and history live on the member, so every instance inherits them — and changing the type changes them all at once.
